answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry resists Sybil attacks by making each identity costly to create: an agent must lock collateral before it can trade, and misbehavior slashes the bond. Like timber that only gains strength as it seasons, reputation accrues slowly through verified work, so a flood of fresh fake identities carries no weight. An atlas of attestations maps each agent history across services, letting peers check whether a newcomer is genuinely established or just spun up. Reaching the zenith of trust therefore demands real time and real capital, pricing mass forgery out of reach.
